title: Line up three cans on shelf marks from shortest to tallest
instruction: put the cans on the shelf marks from shortest on the left to tallest on the right
context: Shelf stocking follows planograms, and many product lines come in one design in several sizes. The robot has to compare heights and order the cans left to right; they look alike from above, so it has to judge height, not colour.
setup: Positions are measured on the table from the midpoint between the two arm bases: forward is away from the arms, left and right as seen from behind the arms. (1) Shelf: a brown strip 12 x 36 cm and 2 mm thick, flat on the table, fixed, centred 33 cm forward on the midline. (2) Marks: three white squares 7 x 7 cm and 2 mm thick on the shelf, fixed, 33 cm forward at 11 cm left, on the midline and 11 cm right. (3) Cans: three red steel cans 5 cm across, alike but for height, loose, standing upright in a row 12 cm forward: the 9 cm can (120 g) at 12 cm left, the 12 cm can (160 g) on the midline and the 6 cm can (80 g) at 12 cm right. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: Scored once, after the episode ends. A can is on a mark if it stands upright (within about 25 degrees of vertical), its centre within the mark's edges and no more than 2 cm above where it rests. 1.0: the 6 cm can is on the left mark, the 9 cm can on the middle mark and the 12 cm can on the right mark. 0.0 otherwise. There is no partial credit: three cans set on the marks at random are in order one time in six, and a single can on its right mark one time in three.
reset_notes: Stand the cans back in their row. The shelf and marks are fixed (tape).
fidelity: Calibrated YAM station replica in Isaac Lab-Arena (Isaac Sim). The shelf and marks are fixed flat boxes; the cans are rigid cylinders of the stated size and mass (no rims or labels). Lighting and cameras follow the station calibration.
